subject: Interpretation of Order Form floor / billing sequencing
messages:
From: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify minimum commitment floor in Order Form

Vanessa / team,

Quick question as we're running procurement review: in the CW_OrderForm_v3.xlsx the Pricing Exhibit shows a "minimum commitment floor" expressed as a monthly token floor and also a quarterly true-up. Our finance team is reading the order form such that the floor applies at invoice time (monthly) and any shortfall is invoiced immediately, whereas our legal folks expected a quarterly true-up window before invoicing. Can you confirm how Redwood interprets the billing sequencing and whether the floor is an "invoiceable event" immediately or allowed a 90-day aggregation?

This matters for our forecast and for how we model credits. If you have a short note or redline recommendation we can run it by our counsel.

Thanks,
Jordan Smirnov
Senior Procurement Manager, CloudWave Systems
[attachment: CW_OrderForm_v3.xlsx (Excel, 36KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smirnov <j.smirnov@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum commitment floor in Order Form

Jordan — thanks for flagging this. Short answer: Redwood's standard commercial intent is to allow a quarterly aggregation/true-up before invoicing for any shortfall tied to a committed minimum (we normally avoid immediate monthly clawbacks for mid-market deals). That said, the language in Exhibit B as currently drafted is ambiguous and could be read as monthly invoiceable.

I attached a quick markup that (1) clarifies the sequencing we want (quarterly true-up window), (2) proposes a soft-credit option for the first quarter to reduce friction, and (3) marks the specific clause we expect legal to sign off on. Can Laura take a look at the redline below and confirm? If you and your counsel are OK with the quarterly true-up we can push the updated exhibit and a DocuSign envelope by end of week.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to confirm redline language and risk posture (internal)
- Karthik to confirm commercial acceptance of soft-credit for Q1
- Jordan to confirm CloudWave counsel OK to proceed on that basis

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
[attachment: pricing-exhibit-markup.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Smirnov <j.smirnov@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum commitment floor in Order Form

Looping in a concise legal-commercial take. Proposed compromise language for Exhibit B, paragraph 3 (new wording in quotes):

"If Customer fails to meet the committed minimum usage over a given calendar quarter, Supplier may invoice the shortfall for that quarter following the end of the quarter; Supplier agrees that no monthly invoicing for shortfalls shall occur prior to the completion of such calendar quarter. For the initial contract quarter only, Supplier will apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the billed shortfall amount to mitigate ramp risk."

Operational notes: this keeps our collections timing standard (quarterly true-up) and gives CloudWave a ramp courtesy. If legal is comfortable, we'll insert a narrow definitions clause referencing "committed minimum" and the metric used (token units) so there is no ambiguity about measurement period. Laura — could you translate the plain-language compromise into tracked-change redline for the document attached?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Sales Ops (Commercial) | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redline-exhibitB.docx (Word, 12KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Smirnov <j.smirnov@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum commitment floor in Order Form

Karthik / team — reviewed and drafted tracked changes. High-level summary of legal position: we can accept the quarterly true-up with the following guardrails to limit future billing disputes:

1) Define measurement basis: "committed minimum" means total billable token units attributed to Customer-generated traffic (excluding development/test, sandbox, and one-off migration credits) measured on a calendar quarter basis.
2) Dispute window: Customer must raise any invoicing dispute within 30 days of receipt of the true-up invoice; undisputed portions remain payable.
3) Audit / evidence: Redwood will provide usage reports and raw token tallies for the quarter as part of the true-up packet; CloudWave may request an audit once per 12 months.
4) Q1 ramp credit: accept the 25% single-use credit as proposed; it applies only to the first completed quarter after production cutover.

I've attached the tracked-change Exhibit B; redline highlights the new definition and the 30-day dispute window. Suggested compromise should keep procurement happy while protecting Redwood from retroactive reclassification of usage.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
[attachment: ExhibitB_redline.pdf (PDF, 22KB)]

From: Jordan Smirnov <j.smirnov@cloudwave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum commitment floor in Order Form

Thanks all — appreciate the clarity and the willingness to add a ramp buffer. CloudWave counsel reviewed Laura's redline overnight and are agreeable to the quarterly true-up with the 30-day dispute window and the Q1 25% credit. Two small asks from our end:

- Could Redwood add an explicit sentence excluding "sandbox/dev" environments from the committed minimum calculation (helps our internal finance mapping)?
- We prefer the true-up invoice to include a line-itemized export (CSV) with per-day token tallies as part of the packet for reconciliation; is that possible operationally?

If you can accept those two minor items we can confirm and request DocuSign. Would like to close by COB Friday the 10th.

Jordan
Senior Procurement Manager | CloudWave Systems
